relevant_observations_paraphrased: The page distinguishes decays of elementary particles from decays of composite particles.
Protons and neutrons are composite particles made of quarks; the neutron has one up and two down quarks, and the proton has two up and one down quark.
In beta-minus decay a neutron changes into a proton and produces an electron and an electron antineutrino. This can occur in a nucleus or for a free neutron.
The beta-minus transformation changes a down quark into an up quark; conservation laws also require the emitted electron and electron antineutrino.
The page discusses the unsettled possibility that neutrinos and antineutrinos may be Majorana particles. Do not infer that the elementary textbook notation settles that research question.
